title: Luceras Legs and Tail
heading: Luceras: legs, paws and tail
lede: Stage 5 of 11, parts 3 to 5. The hind legs, forelegs, all four paws and the tail, on the head and torso you approved: the whole sculpted body. Judge shape only: do the legs, paws and tail read as your shaved clay? Muscle relief and skin texture are surface work the fur covers. Approve, or say what needs work and in which view. Confirm notifies the orchestrator; after this the whole-body check closes the sculpt stage.
fallback: Approvals cannot be saved from this view; reply in chat.
compositeEmpty: Confirm closes the legs, paws and tail; the whole-body check comes next.
confirmed: Confirmed; the orchestrator files it and runs the whole-body check. Tell the orchestrator you confirmed.

fold.title: Decided by the pipeline owner
fold.text: Built by Codex alone from here, with the orchestrator reading every pass against your clay. The hind legs took one pass for the thigh to the hock; the tail and the forelegs were built at the same time as the paws by separate Codex builders and merged by moving only their own points, which worked with nothing refused. The paws took five builds and three method changes: brushing the old foot gave thin pads, then boxes; rebuilding them from pictures of your clay gave mush; building each toe as a tube whose thickness is measured from your clay, the way the tail and horns were made, is the first that reads as your clay's paw. That last lesson is now a pipeline rule. Codex time for these parts about 5 hours, about 1.5M Codex tokens; my reading about 150K Claude tokens.

legs.name: Legs, paws and tail
legs.question: Do the legs, paws and tail read as your shaved clay?
judge: Side: the big hind thigh into the rump, knee, hock, long lower leg, as the clay?
Paws: four rounded toes with clefts, dark claws from the tips?
Forelegs: lean columns, elbow point, wrist, short bone into the paw?
Tail: thick root, steady taper, low curve, upward hook?
legs.note: Named and left for later: the knuckle bumps on the toes are softer and the toe tops more regular than the clay; a few soft creases where the paws meet the legs; muscle relief softer than the clay everywhere, as on the torso you approved. Fur covers all three.
